The 2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix was a Formula One motor racing event held on 12 December 2021 at the Yas Marina Circuit in Abu Dhabi. It was the 22nd and final round of the 2021 Formula One World Championship.

The race was notable for its controversial finish involving the deployment of the safety car in the closing laps, which affected the outcome of the Drivers' Championship between Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton.

Background

Going into the final race, Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton were level on points, with Verstappen ahead on countback due to his eight race victories versus Hamilton's eight victories. Hamilton had led for much of the season, while Verstappen mounted a strong challenge with Red Bull Racing.

The race at Yas Marina would decide the championship outcome, making it one of the most anticipated final rounds in recent Formula One history.

Race

Hamilton led from pole position for the majority of the race, looking set to claim his eighth World Drivers' Championship title. Verstappen ran in second, pressuring Hamilton throughout but unable to make a move.

Safety car

On lap 53, Nicholas Latifi crashed his Williams into the barriers at Turn 14, bringing out the safety car with five laps remaining. The incident sparked a sequence of controversial decisions by race director Michael Masi.

Initially, Masi indicated that lapped cars would not be allowed to overtake the safety car, as is standard procedure. However, he then reversed this decision and allowed only the five cars between Verstappen and Hamilton to unlap themselves, leaving others in place.

This allowed Verstappen, who had pitted for fresh soft tyres under the safety car, to line up directly behind Hamilton for a one-lap shootout. Hamilton, meanwhile, was on older hard tyres having not pitted.

Controversy

The FIA Sporting Regulations state that all lapped cars must be allowed to overtake before the safety car returns to the pits. Masi's selective application of this rule drew immediate protests from the Mercedes team.

Verstappen overtook Hamilton on the final lap at Turn 5, claiming his first World Drivers' Championship. The result was confirmed after Mercedes lodged two protests, both of which were dismissed by the stewards.

In the aftermath, the FIA launched an investigation into the race management decisions. Race director Michael Masi was subsequently replaced ahead of the 2022 season, with a new virtual race control system introduced.

Results

Max Verstappen won the race and the World Drivers' Championship. Lewis Hamilton finished second. Carlos Sainz Jr. completed the podium in third place for Ferrari.
